newsitem.title: UK: Orange plans new services as losses narrow.
newsitem.headline: Orange plans new services as losses narrow.

text.p: Orange Plc, Britain's youngest mobile telephone company, said half year losses narrowed by 41 percent on Thursday, adding that it was considering a host of new on-line services to win new customers.

Orange, which became earnings positive for the first time, said pre-tax losses in the half year had narrowed to 74 million pounds ($117.4 million) -- beating most analyst forecasts -- and said it was on track to pre-tax profitability.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBIDTA) jumped to 12 million pounds from a loss of 70 million pounds in the first half of 1996.

Orange, which has about one million customers and covers 95 percent of the population, said it would double to 800 million pounds planned investments to accelerate the expansion of its network and introduce advanced new services.

The company, which plans to make the new investments by end-1999, is considering offering mobile customers services such as Internet browsing, home shopping, on-line newspapers and financial services, narrow-band television, virtual television and video telephony.

"We are confident that the impact of superior coverage, that extends customer expectations, will grow the market faster, increase our market share, widen wirefree usage, increase chargeable usage and average customer revenues and achieve greater profitability," managing director Hans Snook said in a statement.
Revenues per subscriber rose nine percent to 40.16 pounds per month and were running at 500 pounds per year, up 13 percent, from 1996 levels, the group said.
